After spending around £50 on a takeaway order through Deliveroo two of us became unwell following the meal. Given the cost, I had been really looking forward to it which made the experience even more disappointing. I raised the issue appropriately through Deliveroo and was then contacted directly by the restaurant who initially handled the matter professionally and apologetically. I was told they would be “more than happy to oblige” a refund via Deliveroo and was also offered a complimentary meal as a goodwill gesture.

Unfortunately, since then the experience has been extremely frustrating and has dragged on for months on end with very little resolution.

I was repeatedly passed back and forth between the restaurant and Deliveroo with both parties giving conflicting information about who was responsible for processing the refund. Deliveroo stated the restaurant needed to approve it through their system while the restaurant later advised me to contact Deliveroo directly instead. At one stage, Deliveroo even confirmed that the refund had not been approved by the restaurant.

Communication throughout has been incredibly poor. Emails regularly went unanswered for weeks at a time and despite multiple assurances that the issue would be resolved, I am still left without a proper outcome months later.

What has disappointed me most is not even the original issue itself but the lack of consistent communication, accountability and follow-through afterwards. I remained patient and polite throughout the process but being left chasing repeatedly for months has been exhausting and unnecessarily stressful.

It’s a real shame, as I had genuinely been excited for the meal and initially appreciated the restaurant’s willingness to help. However the handling of the situation afterwards has unfortunately let the entire experience down.

The Anti-Hype Review ⭐⭐**
Everyone’s hyping GDK and I hate hype. So I went with zero expectations. Here’s the truth: It’s not magic. It’s just… well-executed. Bread is crispy because they actually toast it. Meat is good because they don’t overcook it. Sauce is light because German doner isn’t supposed to be a mayo bomb. They give extra if you ask, which most places act like you’re insulting them for asking. Metrocenter food court has 20 food stalls, but most taste the same after 3 bites. This one doesn’t. Is it worth the price? If you care about proper doner, yes. If you just want “full pet”, go eat rice. But for actual kebab? Uncommonly good.

Unfortunately, Ramen Ichiramen no longer offers a regular, non-halal Steak Tataki Ramen. Previously, customers could choose between halal and non-halal beef, but now the website states that all beef used in their ramen is halal, leaving customers with no alternative.

I believe this is unfair to customers who, for personal or religious reasons, do not wish to consume halal meat. As a Christian, I do not believe I should be expected to accept a religiously prepared product when I previously had the option to choose otherwise.

I fully respect the right of Muslim customers to choose halal food. However, I believe the same consideration should be given to customers who prefer non-halal meat. Previously, both options were available, but now only halal beef is offered, meaning that customers who do not want halal meat have lost their choice.

In my opinion, a restaurant should respect the different dietary preferences and beliefs of all its customers rather than remove an option that was previously available.

Unfortunately, this change has left me disappointed. I would like to see Ramen Ichiramen reintroduce the non-halal beef option for its Steak Tataki Ramen.

One star due to the loss of choice and the lack of consideration for customers who do not wish to eat halal meat.
